result.title: Confidence scores for gated automation of large language models
result.summary: AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong capabilities in automated decision-making. However, LLMs may produce incorrect answers with high confidence, limiting their applicability in decisions that affect individuals and organizations. Reliable confidence scores are necessary to gate such decisions, and existing estimates are frequently unavailable or too coarse to support effective gating. This work uses supervised learning to train models to predict the correctness of LLM-generated answers, enabling automated confident responses and routing uncertain ones for human review. A linear confidence score head is fitted to the final-layer hidden state of the frozen LLM backbone, and text-only metamodels are trained as an alternative for closed models. All results come from a single 2B-parameter backbone, on graded answers that are about 98% SQuAD and the remainder TruthfulQA. Against multiple baselines, the confidence score head outperforms all baselines and metamodels, automating the largest fraction of the workload at high accuracy targets. Prompted confidence scores can appear well calibrated yet lack the resolution needed for thresholding. Although transferability to unseen datasets is modest, the confidence score head remains the most robust approach. The proposed confidence scoring framework enhances the safety of automating LLM-based agents and can be adapted to gate other properties, including safety or compliance.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作在冻结 LLM 的末层隐状态上拟合线性置信头（并以纯文本 metamodel 作替代），用监督学习预测答案是否正确，从而自动放行高置信回答、将其余转人工复核；实验基于单个 2B 主干和以 SQuAD 为主的文本数据，置信头优于多种基线与 metamodel。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「从最终隐状态读出正确性以驱动停止/转人工」的探针式做法，可供核查 LVR 中 STOP 决策与内部状态是否可信的线索，但属纯文本、无视觉证据筛选，且「提示式置信看似校准却缺乏阈值分辨率」的观察可能与 latent 自评的可靠性评估相关。
